tools.name: get_entry
tools.title: Get an entry
tools.description: One entry, by VHID, short name or Wikidata QID: its public record (title, description, handles, image, URL) and, as `editing`, its current revision, who manages each field and handle (the Wikidata sync or the site), and whether this key may edit it live.

include_platforms.description: Also list the platforms a handle can be on.

short.description: The entry’s short name (`/<short>`), if it has one.

native_name.description: The name in its own script, shown under the title (`川瀬智子`): from the Wikidata item’s name in native language when it is not the title, or as an editor gave it; null for none.

native_name_lang.description: The language code of `native_name` (`ja`, `zh-hant`), as Wikidata gives it; null when none is known.

also_known_as.description: Another name the subject is known by, as an editor gave it (`Amaranta Hank`): the entry’s search snippet says it after the name, before any alias the Wikidata item states. Never from Wikidata; null for none.

entity_type.description: What it is, from its Wikidata item; null when unknown. `entity_kind` says more.

entity_kind.description: The finer kind of thing it is, from its Wikidata item’s classes; null when unknown (an organisation or a brand not yet read since kinds were added reads null until the sync next reads its item). Each kind belongs to one `entity_type`, named beside it below, and each type is also the kind of an entry of that type with no finer one. New kinds may be added: treat an unknown value as its `entity_type`.

verified.description: Verified Handles has verified the entry.

claimed.description: The person or organisation the entry is about has claimed it. Never who.

rev.description: The version of the entry this body was made from: a later change’s is a larger number. A stamp (`GET /api/v1/stamps`) that differs means the entry has changed. To read an entry past every cache (after your own change, say), ask `?v=<rev>` with the rev your change returned.

propose_policy.description: Who may propose a change to the entry, as its page says: `registered`, any signed-in account; `trusted` or `admin`, only accounts with that role, and the page says why; `closed`, nobody, and the entry cannot be claimed. Whether this account may edit it live is the edit context’s (`GET /api/v1/entities/{vhid}/edit-context`). A body cached before this field was added may lack it until the entry next changes.

description.description: The description as sanitised HTML, links to other entries named as they are today.

title.description: The page’s title, underscored (`Draft:` first for a draft).

adapted.description: Present and true when the text has been edited on the site since.

revision.description: The page’s revision the text was taken from: its permalink is `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=<title>&oldid=<revision>`. Absent on a credit from before revisions were kept.

draft.description: Present and true when the page is an English Wikipedia draft (the Draft namespace), not yet an article.

anyOf.description: The English Wikipedia page an entry’s description was taken from: an article, or a draft (`draft: true`).

description_license.description: The description’s licence, as an SPDX id: `CC-BY-SA-4.0` when it was taken from Wikipedia (`description_source` is set), which means crediting the article and sharing alike. Null otherwise: the description is CC0 like the rest of the text.

image.description: The lead image (the same as `images[0].url`), or null.

thumb.description: The lead image at the width a list row draws it (100 CSS pixels), as a path on the site: the width the image is really served at (200 for a Commons picture), never one that redirects. Null when there is no image.

thumb_plate.description: The plate `thumb` is drawn on (the lead image’s `plate`), and always null when `thumb` is. `light` or `dark`: a picture with transparent pixels (a logo, most often), drawn on a plate of that colour so its ink shows in light and dark mode alike. `none`: an opaque picture (a photo), drawn as it is, with no plate. Null while the site has not yet looked at its pixels: decide from the picture itself, as the site’s pages then do.

license.description: An upload’s licence, by id. Null for a Commons image (see `license_name`) or when none was recorded.

license_name.description: The licence’s name, e.g. "CC BY-SA 4.0". Null until it is known.

freely_licensed.description: May be reused under a free licence. Null when no licence is recorded.

credit.description: The credit line to show when reusing the image.

source_page.description: The image’s Wikimedia Commons file page, which states its licence and author.

anyOf.description: Who owns an image and how it may be reused. An entry’s text is CC0 (bar a description taken from Wikipedia); its images are licensed separately, by their owners.

image_rights.description: The lead image’s rights, or null when there is no image.

url.description: The image, as a path on this site (`/img/w/480q75/<id>`).

main.description: True for the lead image, false for the gallery images after it.

license.description: An upload’s licence, by id. Null for a Commons image (see `license_name`) or when none was recorded.

license_name.description: The licence’s name, e.g. "CC BY-SA 4.0". Null until it is known.

freely_licensed.description: May be reused under a free licence. Null when no licence is recorded.

credit.description: The credit line to show when reusing the image.

source_page.description: The image’s Wikimedia Commons file page, which states its licence and author.

image_rights.description: Who owns an image and how it may be reused. An entry’s text is CC0 (bar a description taken from Wikipedia); its images are licensed separately, by their owners.

link.description: Where the image links on the entry page instead of opening the full-screen viewer, or null.

zoom_url.description: The full-screen viewer’s picture, 1600 pixels wide at most, as a path on this site (`/img/w/1600q75/<id>`): what to load when the viewer opens. Null when the image has a `link`, which opens instead.

zoom_max_url.description: The widest picture this site serves of the image, no wider than the original, as a path on this site: what to load once the viewer is zoomed past twice the screen. Null when there is none wider than `zoom_url` (always for a Wikimedia Commons image), or when `zoom_url` is null.

width.description: The original’s width in pixels, or null when it is not known.

height.description: The original’s height in pixels, or null when it is not known.

plate.description: The plate the image is drawn on, as the entry page draws it. `light` or `dark`: a picture with transparent pixels (a logo, most often), drawn on a plate of that colour so its ink shows in light and dark mode alike. `none`: an opaque picture (a photo), drawn as it is, with no plate. Null while the site has not yet looked at its pixels: decide from the picture itself, as the site’s pages then do.

images.description: Every image the entry shows, the lead first. Empty when it shows none.

category.description: How the entry page groups it.

value.description: The handle as stored (a username, an id, a URL). Null for an email address, which is never published as data.

display.description: The label the entry page shows instead of the value, if an editor set one. Null for email.

display_label.description: What the platform calls a handle whose value is an ID, like `Artist page`: the entry page shows it as the card’s main line and the value under it, unless `display` is set. Null for most platforms.

url.description: The profile’s address, built from the platform’s URL pattern. Null for email.

verified.description: Verified Handles has checked that this account belongs to the entry.

checked.description: What Verified Handles’ own handle checker found when it last looked at this account, from the platform’s official API: only on YouTube (channel and handle), Deezer and GitHub, and only for a look at most 7 days old. Absent otherwise. The entry page shows it only for `dead` (“Not found when checked …”) and `renamed`.

verdict.description: `live`: the profile was there. `dead`: the platform did not find it. `renamed`: it answers under another name. `unknown`: the platform gave no answer a rule could read.

now.description: For `renamed`, the name it answers to now, when the platform gave one. A YouTube handle’s is lowercase.

shown_first.description: The entry page shows it before anyone opens anything: true for the accounts above a long list’s “Show N more accounts”, false for the ones folded under it, for the ones a platform’s own “+ N more” holds (a platform with four accounts or more shows its first), for the external identifiers (listed under their own closed heading, unless the entry has nothing else), and for an account the page does not draw.

platform_first.description: The first of the entry’s accounts on its platform, in this order: the one an editor put first, else the one Wikidata marks preferred, else the one whose name is the entry’s, before its regional accounts. Take it as the entry’s main account there.

items.description: One account or identifier of an entry, in the order the entry page shows them. A Wikidata item linked to the entry comes last, as platform `wikidata`.

merged_into.description: Present when the key asked for named an entry that was merged into this one: this entry’s VHID.

anyOf.description: An entry: the same data its page shows, from the same code. Email addresses are masked. The text is CC0, except a description taken from Wikipedia (`description_license`).

entry.description: The entry’s public record, as GET /api/v1/entities/{vhid} answers it. Null for a VHID that is not public (a deleted entry): `editing` says more.

editing.description: With an API key: what the editor loads for this key (GET /api/editor/{vhid}): `baseRevisionId`, `capabilities` (whether it may edit live or propose), `editable`, `handles`, `provenance` (which fields the Wikidata sync manages), `qid`, and `platforms` with include_platforms. Where the key may not open the editor, the route’s `status` and `error`. Absent with no key.

outputSchema.description: One entry: its public record and, with an API key, what the editor would load for it.

tools.name: search_entries
tools.title: Search entries
tools.description: Find entries by name (words match titles, subtitles, descriptions), by Wikidata QID (the entries linked to it) or by VHID (it and the entries linking to it).

query.description: The query as it was read: trimmed and cut to 100 characters.

total.description: How many entries matched in all.

limit.description: The page size used: the `limit` asked for, clamped to the endpoint’s range.

offset.description: The offset used: the `offset` asked for, clamped to 0–10,000.

next_offset.description: The `offset` of the next page, or null when this is the last one. Follow it rather than computing it.

short.description: The entry’s short name (`/<short>`), if it has one.

claimed.description: The person or organisation the entry is about has claimed it. Never who.

entity_kind.description: The finer kind of thing it is, from its Wikidata item’s classes; null when unknown (an organisation or a brand not yet read since kinds were added reads null until the sync next reads its item). Each kind belongs to one `entity_type`, named beside it below, and each type is also the kind of an entry of that type with no finer one. New kinds may be added: treat an unknown value as its `entity_type`.

thumb_plate.description: The plate `thumb` is drawn on (the lead image’s `plate`), and always null when `thumb` is. `light` or `dark`: a picture with transparent pixels (a logo, most often), drawn on a plate of that colour so its ink shows in light and dark mode alike. `none`: an opaque picture (a photo), drawn as it is, with no plate. snippet.description: Plain text from the description around the words that matched, or null when the match was not in it.

highlighted.description: `snippet` is a real excerpt (true), or there is none (false).

tools.name: find_by_handle
tools.title: Find entries by handle
tools.description: Which public entries list a handle or website: “is this an official account, and whose?”. Give url (a profile’s or a website’s address; a website is matched by its site), or platform and value instead. Empty when none. Not for emails.

url.description: A profile’s or website’s address: https://x.com/someone, example.org.

platform.description: The platform’s catalog id, with value: "twitter" for X; YouTube is "youtube_channel" (a UC… id) or "youtube_handle" (@name, without the @).
The platform looked on: the one asked, or the one whose address `url` is.

value.description: The handle looked up, as the site stores one: from `url`, what follows the platform’s address.
The handle as the entry lists it: on a platform that ignores case, its case may differ from the value asked.

verified.description: Whether the handle itself is verified on this entry (not the entry’s own badge).

items.description: An entry that lists the handle.

results.description: Verified handles first, then by VHID; at most 50. Empty when no public entry lists it.

outputSchema.description: The public entries that list a handle.

tools.name: get_entry_history
tools.title: Entry history
tools.description: An entry’s public edit history, newest first.

merged_into.description: Present when the entry was merged into another: that entry’s VHID. The history is still the merged entry’s own.

limit.description: The page size used: the `limit` asked for, clamped to the endpoint’s range.

offset.description: The offset used: the `offset` asked for, clamped to 0–10,000.

next_offset.description: The `offset` of the next page, or null when this is the last one. Follow it rather than computing it.

ref_id.description: The revision’s id: `a<n>` for the history kept from the old wiki, `r<n>` for an edit made since.

kind.description: `archive`: from the old wiki. `forward`: made on Verified Handles.

actor.description: Who made it, as they chose to be named in public; null when they keep their name private.

is_bot.description: Made by an automated process: the Wikidata sync, an import, or an account an administrator has marked as automation (a script or agent). A legacy (archive) revision keeps the old wiki’s own flag.

hidden.description: Always false here: a hidden revision is never in the public history.

deleted.description: Always false here: a deleted revision is never in the public history.

proposer.description: For an approved proposal, who proposed it, as they chose to be named; null otherwise.

actor_id.description: An opaque id for this person, the same wherever they are named, for blocking; null whenever their name isn’t shown to you. Not an account id and can’t be turned into one; may change if the site’s keys are rotated.

proposer_id.description: An opaque id for this person, the same wherever they are named, for blocking; null whenever their name isn’t shown to you. Not an account id and can’t be turned into one; may change if the site’s keys are rotated.

items.description: One revision in an entry’s public history.

outputSchema.description: A page of an entry’s public revision history, newest first.

tools.name: search_commons_images
tools.title: Search Wikimedia Commons
tools.description: Search Wikimedia Commons for an image for an entry; an exact file name finds that file first. Pass a hit’s `token` to set_entry_image as `commons_token`.

token.description: The file, signed for 30 minutes: what `POST /api/media/commons` and the preview take.

commonsPage.description: The file’s page on Commons, with its licence and author.

items.description: A Wikimedia Commons file a search found.

tools.name: update_entry_fields
tools.title: Edit an entry’s text
tools.description: Change an entry’s text fields (title, subtitle, description, short name, native name, also known as, bio, Wikipedia credit) — a live edit. Give only what changes; null clears. The description is HTML. A field changed here leaves the Wikidata sync (hand it back with set_wikidata_ownership). To ask a reviewer instead, use propose_entry_change.

short.description: The short name in the URL; null removes it.

credit_wikipedia_page.description: Credit the description “from Wikipedia”: an English Wikipedia article or draft, by title or address; refused unless the description is mostly the page’s lead.

credit_let_wikidata_manage.description: With a draft in credit_wikipedia_page: false keeps the description site-authored (by default the Wikidata sync takes it).

bio.description: Only on an entry with NO Wikidata item: a person’s date of birth (and optionally birth name and place of birth), each with a source; null removes it. Shown only while they are 18 or over.

birth_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY, as the source gives it.

birth_date_source.description: A source’s address that states it.

native_name.description: The name in its own script, shown under the title (川瀬智子 for Tomoko Kawase); "" or null removes it. Setting it takes it from the Wikidata sync.

also_known_as.description: Another name the subject is known by, said after the name in search snippets; "" or null removes it. Plain text, ≤100 characters.

summary.description: Why, in plain words, for the public history. Never a ticket or backlog ID.

base_revision_id.description: get_entry’s editing.baseRevisionId: a change since is refused as a conflict.

idempotency_key.description: Optional Idempotency-Key: the same key and change within 24 h replays the first result.

dry_run.description: true: a dry run, which wrote nothing. Absent from a real run.

would_send.description: A dry run: the exact request the real run would send (`method`, `path`, any `headers` such as an Idempotency-Key, and its `body`, `form` or `query`), or the requests, in order.

note.description: A dry run: what to do next to make the change, in words.

confirm.description: A dry run of a change that needs it: the exact target to send back as `confirm` with dry_run: false.

replayed.description: A real run with an idempotency_key already used for this change: the first call’s answer, given back; nothing was written now.

may_edit_live.description: A dry run of a live edit: whether this key’s account may edit this entry live.

refused_because.description: A dry run the real run would be refused for: why, in words.

result.description: A real run: the route’s own answer, where the tool adds facts of its own beside it.

outputSchema.description: A dry run (`dry_run: true`): what the change would be and the exact request it would send. A real run: what the route answered.

tools.name: update_entry_handles
tools.title: Add or remove handles
tools.description: Add or remove handles on an entry, or move some to the front — a live edit. Only the handles named are sent, applied to the list as it is at save (an added one goes last; adding one it has, or removing one it lacks, changes nothing). `first` moves the handles it names to the front, in order. A removed handle the Wikidata sync supplied is held back from it. To ask a reviewer instead, use propose_entry_change.

platform_id.description: Catalog id: twitter (X), youtube_channel (UC… id), youtube_handle (name, no @); others in platform_catalog.

display.description: Text shown instead of the value.

remove.description: Handles to take off, by value (an email you may not see: {platform_id: "email", ref}).

tools.description: Propose, for a reviewer, what a Wikidata item says for an entry: its handles, and if asked its label, description and image. From the linked item it hands the values to the sync (unless protected or claimed); from another item it copies them. Handles the entry has are left out.

take.description: Default ["handles"]; title = its label, subtitle = its description.

note.description: Why, in plain words, for the reviewer. Never a ticket or backlog ID; a VHID is fine.

idempotency_key.description: Optional Idempotency-Key: the same key and change within 24 h replays the first result.

dry_run.description: true: a dry run, which wrote nothing. Absent from a real run.

would_send.description: A dry run: the exact request the real run would send (`method`, `path`, any `headers` such as an Idempotency-Key, and its `body`, `form` or `query`), or the requests, in order.

note.description: A dry run: what to do next to make the change, in words.

confirm.description: A dry run of a change that needs it: the exact target to send back as `confirm` with dry_run: false.

replayed.description: A real run with an idempotency_key already used for this change: the first call’s answer, given back; nothing was written now.

may_edit_live.description: A dry run of a live edit: whether this key’s account may edit this entry live.

refused_because.description: A dry run the real run would be refused for: why, in words.

result.description: A real run: the route’s own answer, where the tool adds facts of its own beside it.

outputSchema.description: A dry run (`dry_run: true`): what the change would be and the exact request it would send. A real run: what the route answered.
